title: A department report from groupingBy and partitioningBy

blocks.text: `Collectors.groupingBy(classifier)` groups a stream into a `Map<K, List<T>>`. A second argument, a *downstream* collector, turns each group into something else: a count, an average, a list of names. `Collectors.partitioningBy(predicate)` is the special case with the keys `true` and `false`.
`DeptReport.Employee` is a record `(String name, String dept, int salary)`. Write four static methods in `DeptReport`:

items: `Map<String, Long> headcount(List<Employee> staff)`: the number of employees per department.
`Map<String, Double> averageSalary(List<Employee> staff)`: the average salary per department.
`Map<String, List<String>> namesByDept(List<Employee> staff)`: the employees' names per department, in list order.
`Map<Boolean, List<String>> splitByPay(List<Employee> staff, int threshold)`: under `true`, the names of those paid at least `threshold`; under `false`, the others; both in list order.

blocks.text: With the staff Alice (Engineering, 90000), Bob (Engineering, 85000), Carol (Marketing, 70000), Dave (Marketing, 72000) and Eve (Engineering, 95000):
An average need not be a whole number, a salary may be as large as an `int` allows, a threshold may put everyone on one side, and two employees may share a name.

cases.says: It counts, averages and lists the staff of each department.
It splits the staff's names into those paid at least the threshold and the rest.
An average of 100 and 101 is 100.5, and two salaries of 2,000,000,000 average 2,000,000,000: the division must not be integer division, and the sum must not overflow an int.
The split has a true and a false entry even when one side is empty, as partitioningBy guarantees.
Employees of the same department are counted together even when their department names are separate String objects: keys are compared with equals, not ==.
Names keep the order of the list, not alphabetical order, in both the department lists and the pay split.
Two employees who share a name are still two employees in the headcount.

concepts: groupingBy with a downstream collector counts, averages or maps the members of each group.
partitioningBy always yields both a true and a false entry.
